findings.title: Child-CTA dispatch is not on the NInfer matrix-product route
evidence: src/ops/linear/gguf/ggml_bridge_mmq.cuh:141-172 handles stream-K and launches mul_mat_q<type,J,false> or the BF16 specialization directly; there is no call to upstream launch_mul_mat_q and no child-CTA template argument
third_party/ggml-quants/src/ggml-cuda/mmq.cuh:1814-1839 contains the new child-CTA dispatch only inside upstream launch_mul_mat_q
findings.trigger: Use the NInfer GGUF matrix_product/linear path with Q4_K, J128, SM86 and stream-K conditions
findings.consequence: The candidate two-child launch is not reached by this project route; its flag can be ON while serving still executes the prior single-CTA launch. Any performance or route claim for NInfer is invalid until the actual wrapper is wired to this dispatch or equivalent logic.

findings.title: Regression option does not prove or execute the child-CTA path
evidence: tests/ops/linear/test_gguf.cpp:2750-2754 parses this option and enables q4_mmq_k_stream_regression
tests/ops/linear/test_gguf.cpp:2948-2951 calls run_mmq_real_shape; that invokes ops::linear (lines 2599-2605), which enters the NInfer bridge above
findings.consequence: The test exercises the current public NInfer path and independent Q8_1 oracle, but not the child-CTA launch. It may pass without compiling/executing the intended kernel and cannot qualify its row remap or fixup.

review_notes: The option is default OFF and CMake rejects non-SM86 builds when enabled (src/ops/linear/gguf/sources.cmake:23,336-342).

Within the currently unreachable upstream launcher, code keeps logical I=128 for stream-K fixup sizing and uses child physical I=64; static fixup plane indexing appears intended to scatter both children into the original logical tile. This is not runtime-validated.
Manifest resource numbers and child shared/register thresholds are hypotheses, not compiled resource or achieved-occupancy evidence.
limits: No build, tests, SASS, GPU, or benchmark run.
Static source review cannot establish compilation, exact output, graph parity, safety under runtime scheduling, resource usage, or performance.
